title: Ratify whether German BVL 2017 orientation values rank as sovereign maximum levels; six categories now depend on the answer
repro: The four de_bvl2017_*_cosmetics_general_* rows carry status "guidance impurity limit" in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, not "maximum level" or "statutory limit". Method v2.0 defines the standard as the strictest applicable maximum set by a credible sovereign government, which leaves open whether a national enforcement ORIENTATION value qualifies. The programme has been answering both ways at once. LIVE Category 15 publishes Cd=100, tAs=500 and tHg=100 with type "gov" (provenance regulatory-alignment, i.e. a direct sovereign ML) on de_bvl2017_cd/tas/thg_cosmetics_general_*, and Pb=500 as a read-across from de_bvl2017_pb_toothpaste_500. Categories 2, 13, 14 and 20 on branch feat/standards-outstanding-cats bind the same rows the same way. Category 19 originally ruled the opposite in 65 verbatim occurrences ("not selectable under Method v2.0") and bound China NMPA instead, publishing Pb 10000, Cd 5000, tAs 2000, tHg 1000 - 5x, 50x, 4x and 10x looser than its siblings on identical rows. acceptance_criteria: A recorded ruling states whether a national enforcement orientation value is selectable as a Method v2.0 sovereign anchor, and under what conditions
If selectable: the register status vocabulary is amended so a selectable row is not labelled in a way that invites the opposite reading, and every category cites the ruling

If NOT selectable: Category 15 Cd/tAs/tHg cells lose their regulatory-alignment tags and are re-derived, the live cert pages for the four affected Cat 15 rows are re-rendered, and Categories 2, 13, 14, 19 and 20 are re-anchored

karen_decision: APPROVE: Ruled SELECTABLE. A sovereign national authority's operative enforcement orientation value (e.g. German BVL 2017 cosmetics) IS a Method v2.0 anchor, under four conditions: sovereign authorship, operative enforcement effect, gap-filling only (a real statutory ML always wins; orientation values are selected only where no statutory ML covers the cell or where stricter than all available statutory MLs), and disclosed-as-what-it-is. Rationale: no numbered statutory cosmetic ML exists for most metals in most jurisdictions, so declining orientation values leaves cosmetic cells anchorless or forces forbidden occurrence-derivation; BVL is stricter than the binding national regimes (China NMPA, Korea MFDS), so adopting it is the strictest-applicable (conservative) choice; and it is the reading already in production (live Cat 15 tags BVL regulatory-alignment). No published value moves. Recorded durably in docs/governance/orientation-values-selectability-2026-08-17.md. Reversal blast radius (re-derive live Cat 15 Cd/tAs/tHg + re-anchor 2/13/14/19/20) documented in the ruling.

title: Ratify DOI granularity as two-tier (per-subcategory Standard DOI + per-category manual/Series grouping); reject category-level and flat per-subcategory
repro: A 4-lens adversarial audit (2026-08-31: legal, metadata, dependency-breakage, steelman) rejected the interim category-level (one-DOI-per-category) recommendation. Grounds: certification binds to the SUBCATEGORY standard, not the category (content/verify.md:49,56,60; content/standards/index.md declares 'Seafood 3.1' and 'Culinary Oils and Fats 3.1' different standards, each its own page); the ratified Certification-Readiness ruling REGISTERED clause says 'the standard has a resolvable production DataCite DOI', scoped to the subcategory exactly like COMPLETE/CORRECTED (governing-principles 3.2); per-subcategory DOIs are the already-ratified+shipped plan (rail_box on all 348 standard pages promises per-standard DOIs; DOI-MINTING-LEDGER.md:59,65). The category-level argument was an equivocation (readiness is ASSESSED per category; that is not the same as the DOI ATTACHING per category). Two-tier dominates: per-subcategory Standard DOIs (concept + version chain on material revisions only) GROUPED under the category via the manual Report DOI (IsPartOf/HasPart) where a manual exists (cats 1,3,6,17,24) or a DataCite Series container where not. It captures the certified atom AND the document-of-record; needs NO readiness-lint inheritance rewrite; needs NO ruling re-ratification (the ledger already carries both hmtc.std.cat.slug and hmtc.manual.cat suffixes); and is LESS work than category-level (Series grouping is a metadata field, not 30 net-new thin category landing pages).

title: DataCite mint infrastructure is not defensibility-ready — 3 gates + 2 safety bugs before any production mint (frozen deposits, version chain+dates, identity firewall)
repro: Legal + metadata adversarial audits (2026-08-31): minting on the current tooling would be a net defensibility NEGATIVE at any granularity. GATE 1 (frozen deposits): all 348 standards carry cert_doi:null; a minted DOI would resolve to a live, silently-editable page on the certifier own domain, with no immutable snapshot behind it. A DOI courtroom value is a third-party, tamper-evident version history; without a frozen deposit the mint buys the manufactured-authority attack and none of the upside. Cat-1 v1 (Zenodo, CERN-run frozen PDF) is currently MORE independent than the planned self-run 10.83138 prefix pointing at heavymetalcertified.com, so migrating the DOI-of-record to the self-run prefix is an independence downgrade unless a neutral external frozen deposit is retained. GATE 2 (version chain + dates): buildPayload (tools/mint-dois.mjs:224-251) emits only a version string, one References relatedIdentifier, NO dates array and NO IsNewVersionOf chain; publicationYear is derived from effective_date (:202) which can predate the real mint (never backdate). Must emit dates [Issued = true mint date] and the concept/version chain. GATE 3 (identity firewall): Karen is the sole creator on BOTH the index literature prefix (10.83376) and the cert standards prefix (10.83138) under one DataCite membership; the public DataCite graph therefore impeaches the two-independent-properties firewall (Part 2), and Paleo Certified, Inc. (the IP owner of record, Part 14) appears nowhere as rightsHolder. SAFETY BUG A: DATACITE_MODE=live with --state=draft would stamp non-resolvable draft DOIs into cert_doi (DOI-MINTING-LEDGER.md:185-189). SAFETY BUG B: mint-dois emits no container while datacite-preflight rehearses container {type Series} (mint/preflight drift).

title: Define DOI-mint Rule #1 '95% confidence' = firm-by-occurrence OR firm-by-sovereign-ML OR disclosed-read-across; NOT 95% occurrence for all 9 analytes (impossible under Method v2.0)

So DOI-mint Rule #1 ('every subcategory >=95% confidence in the numbers') cannot mean '95% occurrence confidence on all 9 analytes' — that is impossible for every category and would make the whole program un-mintable. Rule #1 must mean each cell is FIRM: an occurrence percentile at >=95% confidence where occurrence binds (Tier-1 toxics), OR a sovereign government ML (a lookup, definitionally firm), OR a disclosed read-across.

But tools/mint-dois.mjs generateSuffix() emits hmi.<category>.<slug>.<8-hex-hash>. If run in DATACITE_MODE=live for any NEW page it will mint in a DIFFERENT scheme than the established namespace, and hmi.<basename> risks cross-directory basename collisions (synthesis vs metals). Frontmatter for the 24 pages was just backfilled from the registry, so the tool now idempotently SKIPS them (wiki_doi non-null) — this is latent risk for future mints only, not live breakage.
acceptance_criteria: generateSuffix() emits hmi.<slug-basename> matching the 24 live DOIs, OR a documented decision records why the scheme differs

title: FDA Monograph M016 permits talc at 45 to 100 percent in an OTC skin protectant with no contaminant limit, and the baby-powder synthesis regulatory section does not cite it
repro: While revising the diaper-cream synthesis for SYN-REV-1 I read fda2021-otc-monograph-m016-skin-protectant (Final Administrative Order OTC000005, effective 2020-03-27). Section M016.10(p) permits talc at 45 to 100 percent of an OTC skin-protectant drug product, and the order states no heavy-metal contaminant limit for any listed active. The regulatory section of wiki/synthesis/heavy-metals-in-baby-lotions-oils-and-powders.md (PR 179) discusses US instruments reaching a talc baby powder and cites 21 CFR 73.1550 talc colour-additive and the JECFA food-additive spec, but not M016. A US talc baby powder marketed as a skin protectant falls inside M016, so the page's statement that no US instrument sets a finished-product number for talc is correct but under-evidenced: M016 is the instrument that most directly governs the article and is silent on contaminants. Not retrofitted because PR 179 was already open and the SYN-REV-1 order scoped each PR to one page.
acceptance_criteria: The regulatory-landscape section of the baby-powder synthesis cites fda2021-otc-monograph-m016-skin-protectant with the talc 45 to 100 percent range and the absence of a contaminant limit

title: Commit lock hook aborts on Linux because it is bash sourced from dash
repro: Husky runs .husky/pre-commit with dash. The hook sources tools/autonomy/commit-lock.sh, which uses bash [[. On Linux, an existing lock dir then takes the ownerless branch and runs stat -f, which prints a filesystem report instead of an mtime. The arithmetic aborts the hook with Illegal number. A dead holder left .git/hmi-commit.lock.d behind after the chocolate thin-page commits.
acceptance_criteria: A commit on Linux with a leftover lock dir either acquires the lock or reclaims it, and the hook exits 0 without requiring HMI_SKIP_COMMIT_LOCK.
notes: Not fixed in the chocolate direct-answer pass. The stuck lock dir was removed locally so the OpenAlex retry commit could land.
